Homogenize Bins of a Dataframe

Source: R/pb_helpers.R
optimize_bin_max.Rd

optimize_bin_max() splits every bin that holds more than max_allowed points. The points of the bin get the number of bins that method and drop give for them (estBinSize()) and are divided into that many bins of equal width over their range; the first new bin starts at the lower bound of the bin and the last ends at its upper bound, so that the new bins cover the bin without gaps. The other bins are kept.

optimize_bin_max(
  bin_table,
  max_allowed,
  verbose = TRUE,
  time_vector,
  lbound,
  ubound,
  bin.size,
  method,
  drop
)

Arguments

bin_table

A dataframe containing the bin data.

max_allowed

The maximum allowed size for a bin: a bin with more points is split.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, prints detailed output.

time_vector

A vector representing time or a sequence that bins refer to.

lbound

The name of the lower bound column in bin_table.

ubound

The name of the upper bound column in bin_table.

bin.size

The name of the bin size column in bin_table.

method

The rule that gives the number of new bins (see estBinSize()).

drop

The factor that multiplies that number (drop_fac).

Value

A dataframe with adjusted bins. The structure of the dataframe will be the same as bin_table with updated values for the bin size and bounds.

Details

sc.squeeze() passes as max_allowed the maximum of Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.2: the mean plus the standard deviation of the sizes of all bins of the path, set once from the bins of the rule. "Bins larger than the maximum size are divided", and "The process is repeated until all bins conform to the established size criteria": sc.squeeze() calls optimize_bin_max() again, with the same max_allowed, until no bin is larger.
